newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish funds draw record investments - paper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish funds draw record investments - paper.

text.p: Swedish share funds of all types drew 24.6 billion crowns in new deposits in the first two months of 1997, more than the combined total for the two full years of 1995 and 1996, business daily Dagens Industri said on Friday.

Quoting the Swedish Association of Funds, it said that the biggest draws were equity-based funds, whose receipts were expected to continue growing in March with liquidity moving into equities from a bond market with much lower yields than a couple of years ago.

In February, unit trusts -- including public savings schemes -- attracted 8.2 billion crowns in net investment while fixed-interest funds got only 0.5 billion in fresh liquidity. Mixed funds drew new investments of 1.8 billion, it said.
Analysts said that the main reason for the boom was a flood of new liquidity coming from maturing bonds.
"(Money from) maturing non-government bonds worth almost 20 billion crowns is largely expected to cross to equity funds," Per Axelson, of savings bank Swedbank told Dagens Industri.
"This is money from the large number of bonds issued over the past five years which are maturing during the first six months of 1997," an analyst told Reuters.
